predecessors.name: Duchy of Burgundy
predecessors.text: the Nivernais, administered by Otto-William before 990

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the county of Nevers, raised to a duchy in the peerage of France in 1539

rulers.name: Matilda II and Odo of Burgundy

ledger.x: 989: Landry of Monceaux becomes the first hereditary Count of Nevers.
1002: Landry takes Auxerre in the succession war over the duchy.
1003: King Robert II's army fails before Auxerre.

1005: Robert II makes peace with Landry after two unsuccessful sieges of Auxerre and the surrounding area (the page's account, paraphrased; Robert had called on Duke Richard II of Normandy for troops).
1031: Renaud I succeeds Landry (the Auxerre page has Renauld from 1028).

1184: Peter II of Courtenay, husband of Countess Agnes I (1181-1192), shares the county; the Courtenay house enters the line (List page: Peter II 1184-1192; the Auxerre page has him as count of Auxerre 1184-1218).
1199: Hervé IV of Donzy enters the line beside Matilda I (countess 1192-1257); the List page gives Hervé 1199-1223 and Guigues IV of Forez 1226-1241 without stating their relation to her.
1257: Matilda II and her husband Odo of Burgundy hold the county (List page: both 1257-1262, also counts of Auxerre); Yolande II follows in 1262-1280.
1272: Robert III of Flanders holds the county (List page: Robert III 1272-1280, count of Flanders 1305-1322; father of Louis I, who follows in 1280-1322).
1322: Louis I of Flanders becomes Count of Nevers and Flanders; the county is ruled with Flanders until 1384.

1384: Nevers and Rethel pass to Philip the Bold with the Flanders inheritance: 'Cet héritage est réalisé en 1384', covering Flanders, the County of Burgundy and 'des comtés de Nevers et de Rethel (fiefs français)'.
1407: Philip II takes Nevers and Rethel as his own.
1491: the Cleves line takes the county.
1539: the county of Nevers is raised to a duchy in the peerage of France.

wars.name: Succession war for the Duchy of Burgundy
wars.outcome: Two unsuccessful royal sieges of Auxerre and its area; Robert II made peace with Landry in 1005.

wars.name: Battle of Agincourt
wars.outcome: Count Philip II of Nevers and Rethel was killed on 25 October 1415; his son Charles I, born 1414, succeeded.

certainty.note: A feudal county with no treaty or survey line on any page; the outline is the Nivernais with the Auxerre area, as Cliopatria draws it.

sources.title: List of counts and dukes of Nevers
